name: Microsoft Corporation

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.why: Google Cloud vs Azure; Workspace vs Microsoft 365; AI models

peers.name: Oracle
peers.why: Cloud infrastructure and database for the same enterprises; AI data centres

valuation.vl3_basis: trailing P/E, 5 years (price / last-12-month SEC diluted EPS), labelled; GAAP EPS includes OpenAI gains/losses (about +4% to the last 12 months as of Jun-26)

dm4.name: Azure growth (constant currency)
dm4.measured_against: Microsoft's own guidance for that quarter (midpoint), growth vs the same quarter a year earlier
dm4.what: How fast Microsoft's cloud computing business (Azure) is growing vs the same quarter last year, excluding currency moves.
dm4.why: Azure is where the AI spending goes (about $175bn of capex planned for calendar 2026, including leases); its growth must stay high to pay that back.
dm4.bull_means: Azure met or beat Microsoft's own guidance.
dm4.neutral_means: Azure fell short of guidance by less than 3 points.
dm4.bear_means: Azure missed Microsoft's own guidance by 3 points or more: the AI payback story is slipping.
dm4.threshold_rule: Kenneth, 6 Oct 2026: bullish at or above the guide midpoint, bearish 3+ points below it. Jun-26 quarter guide 39-40% -> lines 39.5% / 36.5%. Sep-26 quarter guide ~45% -> lines 45% / 42% when that result is scored (update at each results).

dm4.name: Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud growth (constant currency)
dm4.latest: +14% constant currency (Q4 FY26); +16% on Microsoft's adjusted basis
dm4.what: Growth in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue (Office, Teams, Copilot sold to companies) vs a year earlier, excluding currency moves.
dm4.why: It is Microsoft's most profitable, most recurring revenue, and shows whether Copilot is lifting what customers pay.
dm4.bull_means: Office is still growing in the mid-teens: price rises and Copilot are working.
dm4.bear_means: Office growth has slowed: AI is not adding to what customers pay.

dm5.name: AWS + Google Cloud combined revenue growth
dm5.source: Amazon and Alphabet quarterly results (AWS segment, Google Cloud segment)
dm5.measured_against: same calendar quarter a year earlier
dm5.what: Combined revenue growth of Microsoft's two big cloud rivals, AWS and Google Cloud, vs the same quarter a year earlier.
dm5.why: It shows whether demand for cloud and AI computing is growing across the whole market, independent of Microsoft's own reporting.
dm5.bull_means: The whole cloud market is booming (30%+).
dm5.neutral_means: Cloud demand is growing at a normal pace.
dm5.bear_means: Cloud demand has slowed to 20% or less, as in the 2023 slowdown.

overrides.reason: Kenneth, 5 Oct 2026: Microsoft is valued as a cloud platform, so only the three hyperscale cloud rivals are a like-for-like comparison. Accepted risk: with 3 peers the median is the middle company, so one stale or distorted forecast moves VL1, VL2, VL4 and PT4. Listed under Known defects.

mix._note: Revenue mix (plan section 'Revenue mix', not scored). match = patterns on the row label printed in the SEC filing. Microsoft reports operating income for 3 segments only, so each part shows its segment's operating margin (marked *).

segments.name: Dynamics & Microsoft 365 consumer
match: ^(dynamics products and cloud se|microsoft consumer products an)$

mix.note: Microsoft reports operating income for its 3 segments only (Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, More Personal Computing), so each part shows its segment's operating margin (*). Windows, Xbox and search are shown together as the More Personal Computing segment because Microsoft renamed the Xbox and search rows in its FY26 annual report, so their Jun-26 quarter cannot be derived separately. Microsoft re-drew its segments in Aug 2024 (restated back to Sep-23); stage D reads the last 8 filings (n=8) so only quarters on the new basis are used.
